decisionsTitle: Four small asks: Girl Zone's address, Mailgun or Gmail per form, an optional email beside the name, the calendar fold
decisionsSection:
**The owner, the evening of 2026-10-14**, four asks (and «YOLO»: the open points are decided here, and said). No migration.

**1. Girl Zone's address is `?tip=girl-zone` (amends §676).** «`?tip=siguranta` trebuie să fie `?tip=girl-zone`». The safety branch's slug is `girl-zone` in both languages (the slug was never localized: one word for the link a club shares or an email carries). `siguranta` stays a **read alias** (`BRANCH_SLUG_ALIASES`): `?tip=siguranta` and `?sent=siguranta` on the wizard answer a redirect to the same query written with `girl-zone` — every other word of it kept (`aliasRedirect`, on a GET only, a plain `redirect`, never a permanent one, so no browser keeps it) — so a link already in a sent email or on paper keeps working. Every address the code builds (`BRANCH_SLUG`: the refusal's, the sent page's, the step-1 choice, the thank-you's) writes the new word; the alias lookup is an own-property test, so `toString` or `__proto__` in the address bar is no branch. Code identifiers do not change (§676 refused it, still): the branch is `safety`, the setting key `feedbackForms`.

**2. «Prin ce trimitem»: the road is the club's choice, per form (amends §676, §678 and §149's «Girl Zone only by Mailgun»).** «Aici trebuie să setăm prin ce trimitem mail (Mailgun sau Gmail)». Each of the four forms has a road, `gmail` — the club's account over SMTP, the one «Scrie-ne» leaves by (§149) — or `mailgun` — the environment's sender. It is a field of the form's entry in the existing `platform_settings` row (`feedbackForms`), so no migration; a row saved before has none and reads as the form's default, which is **exactly what §676 fixed in code: Gmail for «Cum a fost», «O sugestie» and «O reclamație», Mailgun for Girl Zone**. On «Pagini» → «Contact» → «Spune-ne ceva», under each form's recipient, two native radios (`RadioField`, never a toggle; it gained a `disabled`): «Gmail-ul clubului („Scrie-ne”)» and «Mailgun», each with a line saying what it does. The save is audited as a word (`viaChanged`: which form, to which road — never an address). **A road the deployment lacks** (`feedbackRoads`: Gmail where `CONTACT_FORM_MODE` is not `off`, Mailgun where `EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE` is not `capture`, a laptop and the tests excepted) is greyed with the sentence and a link to its steps in «Sarcini» (the rows `contactForm` and `liveEmail` — the card showed no readiness of its own, so it computes this one); it stays checked when it is what was saved. A greyed radio is never posted, so a save that posts none keeps the road already saved (`keepUnpostedVia`), and the service refuses to *newly* choose a road the deployment lacks, on the form's box. A form whose road is missing is not offered on the site, as the three were not without the SMTP road. **Which road carries a message** follows the form whose reader it reaches (`roadBranch`): a message for the club's mailbox leaves by the road of the form it was written on — a Girl Zone message the sender gave «Clubul» by «O reclamație»'s, whose mailbox it reaches — and a message for the designated person by Girl Zone's own, whatever form it was written on. With the defaults that is §678 to the letter. A confidential report's typed address is never handed to the spam screen (`senderEmail` is empty for Girl Zone, as before this release), so a lookalike domain cannot mark it «[posibil spam]». Screening is by the reader, not the road: a message for the club's mailbox is marked «[posibil spam]» or held back on the Administrator's tick (§310, §744) on either road, a message for her never. Mailgun sends one message per recipient (the allowlist and the allowance count addresses one by one) and counts as sent when any took it. **Girl Zone by Gmail** puts her messages in the club's mailbox and the account's Sent folder, which everybody who reads it sees: the card says so in one line under Girl Zone's radios — «Prin Gmail, mesajul Girl Zone rămâne în căsuța clubului și îl văd cei care o citesc; prin Mailgun ajunge doar la persoana de mai sus» — so her confidentiality is the club's choice. The footer says the road is chosen per form.

**Girl Zone's Gmail waits on the privacy notice (a marker, `{{feedbackSafetyGmail}}`).** The notice in force promises her messages reach the designated person «fără să treacă prin căsuța clubului»; that is false the day the club ticks Gmail for her, and the house gates every change in where a person's data goes on the approved notice (AGENTS.md §10.8; §562, §613, §678, §754). The template's feedback paragraph now carries the exception — «afară de cazul în care clubul alege, pentru mesajele ei, {{feedbackSafetyGmail}} (secțiunea 6)», in both languages — and the marker is filled with «Gmail-ul clubului» / “the club's Gmail” (`feedbackSafetyGmailClause`, `Tell.noticeSafetyGmail`). `describesFeedbackSafetyGmail` reads it, in every language (`noticeDescribesFeedbackSafetyGmail`, `cachedFeedbackSafetyGmailDescribed`). Until a notice carrying it is in force: Girl Zone's Gmail radio is greyed with a sentence and a link to «Texte legale»; `updateFeedbackSettings` refuses to *newly* choose it, on Girl Zone's box (a saved Gmail may stay, as a missing road may); `effectiveFeedbackSettings` makes her road Mailgun wherever a message leaves or a visitor is told who reads it, whatever the row says; and `/admin/tasks` carries the row `feedbackSafetyGmailNotice`, only while Gmail is the saved road for her, open until the notice names it and done by itself after. The ordinary forms' Gmail needs no marker: the club's mailbox is what the notice already names for them (section 6). **What a visitor is told follows the road:** «doar la {name}» (`Tell.safety.reader`, `readerChoice`, `sent.safety`, `audience.personHint`) is said only on Mailgun; on Gmail each has a twin (`…Gmail`) that says the message reaches her through the club's mailbox, where whoever reads it sees it too — never «doar» or «Confidențial» without the caveat.

**3. The optional email beside the name (amends §678).** «Și dacă aleg „nume și prenume” ar trebui să fie și un mail opțional». **It was already there** on the three ordinary forms since §678 («E-mail (opțional)», shown with the name by CSS alone, always present without scripts, dropped server-side from an anonymous post, `Reply-To` by the SMTP road); **Girl Zone alone had no box called email** — one free «way back» line for an email or a telephone — so the ask changed nothing the owner could see on the form he was opening. Girl Zone's named mode now has the same «E-mail (opțional)» box (field `email`, the message's `Reply-To`) and, beside it, «Telefon (opțional)» (field `contact`, carried in the message and no `Reply-To`): one box per purpose. An address typed in the telephone box still answers (a draft or a link from before keeps working). The message's «Contact» line joins the two. What the ask also needs to be true: the address is validated through the **versioned canonicalizer** (AGENTS.md §10.4; `z.email()` first, then `canonicalizeEmail`, what is kept is the typed address trimmed — capitals and a `+tag` are the person's own), so «Ana <ana@…>», two addresses, a zero-width character or a bare `+tag@gmail.com` are refused on the box with the box's name, kept from the sealed draft; the typed address is the message's `Reply-To` **on both roads** (the adapter gained a per-message `replyTo`, a bare address, never the typed name — which would be a header; Mailgun's `noReplyTo` still outranks it and is what an anonymous or address-less message carries, so nobody is answered at the shared mailbox by default); on Girl Zone the email box is the `Reply-To`, the telephone none. **Nothing is stored:** no table, no outbox row, no audit row, no bucket key (the hourly bucket is the branch's), no log word; the footer's «site-ul nu păstrează niciun mesaj» stays true. **Does the notice in force have to name it first? No** — the named mode itself is gated on `{{feedbackFormsNamed}}` in the notice in force (§678) and exists only while it names it; the email is a box of that mode, and the template's feedback paragraph already said «împreună cu un e-mail sau un telefon, dacă vrei să-ți răspundem». The template now says «(opțional)» and that the email becomes the message's reply address and the platform does not keep it; a notice approved before has the older, still-true sentence, so no new gate.

**4. «Adaugă în calendar» is one pill (amends §767).** «Asta ar trebui să fie collapsed, că nu vedem tot șirul de opțiuni». The five doors stay, in §767's order and words, behind **one small pill** — the share row's own 28-pixel pill with its tap band (`SHARE_PILL_SX`) drawn on the `<summary>` of a native `<details>`, closed on arrival: the calendar glyph, «Adaugă în calendar», a chevron that turns when it opens; the border and the hover take the outlined button's own tokens (half the primary colour, a primary tint), so the pill and the five doors it opens read as kin. No island and no MUI `Menu`: it opens with a click, Enter or Space, and with scripts off. Open, the five pills wrap on one line under it, then the file's note (§674) and the file's address fold (a fold inside the fold), all moved inside so the closed page shows one small control; the share row «Dă mai departe» is unchanged and stays above. The summary's words lost their colon (a caption's colon is not a pill's).

**Refused.** A localized slug for Girl Zone (§676's one-word-both-languages reasoning stands). A permanent redirect for the alias. Renaming the code's `safety` or the setting key. A second road as a fallback when the chosen one refuses (the Mailgun that replaces Girl Zone's Gmail until the notice names it is the notice's own promise, not a retry) — «Nu am putut trimite acum…» with the text kept, as before; a message that falls to Gmail after Mailgun refuses defeats the choice. A single mixed «email or telephone» line on Girl Zone (replaced by two boxes, one purpose each).
changelogLine: - **Four small asks** — Girl Zone's address is `?tip=girl-zone` (`siguranta` still opens it), each «Spune-ne ceva» form has a «Prin ce trimitem» choice between the club's Gmail and Mailgun (Girl Zone's Gmail waits for a privacy notice that names it), the optional email beside the name — on Girl Zone's form too — is checked and becomes the reply address on either road, and «Adaugă în calendar» is one small pill that opens the five doors. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Girl Zone's form is addressed `?tip=girl-zone` in both languages, in every address the code builds (the choice, a refusal's, the sent page's); `?tip=siguranta` and `?sent=siguranta` answer a redirect to the same query written with `girl-zone`, every other word of it kept, and an unknown word, `toString` or `__proto__` is no branch. Tested in tests/unit/feedback/branches.test.ts and tests/e2e/feedback.spec.ts (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Under each of the four forms on «Pagini» → «Contact» → «Spune-ne ceva», «Prin ce trimitem» is a pair of native radios — «Gmail-ul clubului („Scrie-ne”)» and «Mailgun» — saved in the existing `feedbackForms` setting and audited as a word; the default is Gmail for the three and Mailgun for Girl Zone, so a row saved before reads as it did; a road the deployment lacks is greyed with a link to its steps in «Sarcini», kept when it is what was saved and refused when newly chosen; a form whose road is missing is not offered; a message leaves by the road of the form whose reader it reaches, with the same screening by either road, Mailgun with tracking off and Gmail unchanged; Girl Zone carries a one-line note that Gmail means the club's mailbox readers see the message, and the card's footer says the road is chosen per form; Girl Zone's Gmail is greyed, refused when newly chosen, and replaced by Mailgun where a message leaves, until the privacy notice in force names `{{feedbackSafetyGmail}}` in every language (the row `feedbackSafetyGmailNotice` in «Sarcini»), and on Gmail the visitor's words about who reads her message never say «doar»; a confidential report's typed address is not given to the club's spam screen. Tested in tests/integration/feedback/submit.test.ts, tests/unit/feedback/branches.test.ts, tests/unit/feedback/feedback-forms-panel.test.ts and tests/unit/feedback/identity-choice.test.ts, tests/unit/diagnostics/owner-tasks.test.ts and tests/e2e/feedback.spec.ts (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Where a person chooses to give their name — on Girl Zone's form too, beside a «Telefon (opțional)» box — the optional «E-mail (opțional)» box is validated through the versioned canonicalizer (an address it refuses is refused on the box, and kept from the sealed draft), is the message's `Reply-To` by Gmail and by Mailgun  and is stored nowhere: no table, no outbox or audit row, no bucket key. The privacy notice's template says the email is optional and becomes the message's reply address; the notice in force need not name it first, the named mode being gated on `{{feedbackFormsNamed}}`. Tested in tests/integration/feedback/submit.test.ts, tests/unit/feedback/branches.test.ts and tests/e2e/feedback.spec.ts (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criteria 45 and 47: on an event page, «Adaugă în calendar» is one small pill — the share row's 28-pixel pill with its glyph, the words and a chevron — that is the summary of a native fold closed on arrival; open, the five doors (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook.com, Outlook for work or school, the `.ics`) wrap on one line under it in the subscription panel's words and order, followed by the file's note and the file's address fold (inside it); it opens by click, Enter or Space and with scripts off, and the share row above is unchanged. Tested in tests/unit/events/share-row-calendars.test.ts, tests/e2e/share-links.spec.ts and tests/e2e/members-only.spec.ts (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 233: the calendar row's closed state is one summary pill, 28 pixels with the 36-pixel tap band, inside the page at 320 pixels; its five doors, once open, wrap there (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN). Tested in tests/e2e/share-links.spec.ts.
